correctness.rationale: The two closed-neighborhood identities are exact and immediately reduce feasibility to the extreme pair differences. The exact-range Laurent decomposition is disjoint and exhaustive, and the threshold truncation is precisely the proved criterion. An independent implementation path exhaustively checks all 597,780 labelings for 3<=n<=6 and matches every tested bivariate and weight coefficient.

value.rationale: Deleting a perfect matching from a complete bipartite graph creates a natural pair-indexed perturbation of a classical domination-function family. The theorem identifies the exact new sufficient statistics—two side sums and the extreme matched-pair differences—and converts them into a complete function enumerator and a natural optimum-function classification. This is materially finer than a scalar minimum and exposes the structural effect of the deletion.
